ch01.description: TPU history from v1 to Ironwood and TPU 8t/8i, and roofline analysis: arithmetic intensity, ridge points and compute-bound batch sizes against H100.
objectives: I can explain each TPU generation, from v1 to 8t and 8i, as a response to a named bottleneck.
I can compute the math time, the communication time and the ridge point for any chip from its spec sheet, and state which regime a kernel is in.
I can derive that a bf16 matmul's arithmetic intensity is about its token batch, and give the compute-bound batch for v5e, Ironwood, H100 and TPU 8i.
I can show why int8 or fp8 weights with bf16 math halve the compute-bound batch, and why fp8 math doubles it again.
I can apply the same roofline to an interconnect link and derive when a sharded matmul is communication-bound.
I can name what the HBM roofline leaves out (VPU-bound ops, latency-bound transfers, achievable fraction of peak) and when each matters.
teachback: Your H100 intuition says a decode step at batch 64 is memory-bound. Show on a whiteboard whether that holds on Ironwood, and at what batch it stops holding.
Why did Google build an inference-only chip first, then a training chip, then split into two chips again in 2026? Name the bottleneck each time.
Why does int8 weights with bf16 math lower the compute-bound batch, while int8 math does not?
From TPUv2 to Ironwood, FLOPs per chip grew 50× and HBM bandwidth 10.5×. What does that do to the batch you need, and what did Google build to compensate?

ch02.description: Inside a TPU TensorCore: MXU systolic arrays, VPU, VMEM scratchpad, (8,128) tiling, SparseCore and megacore, mapped against the NVIDIA SM model.
objectives: I can draw a TensorCore and say what each unit does — scalar unit, VPU, MXU, XLU, VMEM, SMEM, vector registers and DMA engines — and which one issues instructions to the rest.
I can explain weight-stationary systolic dataflow and compute an MXU tile's utilization from M, K, N and the array size.
I can explain why a contraction or output dimension smaller than the array, or not a multiple of it, wastes MXU capacity, and estimate the waste.
I can explain why VMEM is a compiler-managed scratchpad rather than a cache, give its size per generation, and compute the ridge point for VMEM-resident weights.
I can explain (8,128) tiling and the bf16 and int8 packing, and what they imply for array shapes.
I can say how many devices JAX sees per chip on v4, v5e, v5p, v6e, Ironwood, 8t and 8i, and why.
I can say what SparseCores and 8i's Collectives Acceleration Engine are for.
I can map SM, warp scheduler, CUDA core, shared memory, Tensor Core and HBM onto TPU units, and name three places the mapping breaks.
teachback: A GPU hides memory latency with up to 64 resident warps per SM. What hides it on a TPU, and what does that imply for who has to be clever?
Google moved from 128×128 to 256×256 matrix units in v6e. What does that buy, and what does it cost a model with head dimension 64?
What is VMEM, how big is it on Ironwood and on 8i, and why did 8i triple it?
Why does a decode step leave the matrix units mostly idle even if the weights were already on chip?

sources.label: GPUs vs TPUs at the chip level

ch03.description: TPU interconnect: ICI links, 3D torus and wraparound, optical circuit switches, slices, pods, DCN multislice and TPU 8i Boardfly, compared with NVLink.
objectives: I can describe the TPU topologies — a 2D torus on v5e and v6e, OCS-joined 4×4×4 cubes forming a 3D torus on v4, v5p and Ironwood, and Boardfly on 8i — and say which slice shapes have wraparound.
I can convert a Cloud-docs ICI figure (per chip, both directions, all links) into per-link one-way bandwidth and into the per-axis bandwidth used in collective cost formulas.
I can explain what optical circuit switches buy (reconfiguration, failure isolation, non-contiguous and twisted slices) and what they cost.
I can rank HBM, ICI, PCIe and DCN for Ironwood with numbers, and say which parallelism belongs on each.
I can compute hop counts, diameter and point-to-point transfer time on a slice, and say when a transfer is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound.
I can explain why TPU 8i abandons the torus for Boardfly, using hop latency and decode traffic.
I can compare TPU scale-up with NVLink domains and InfiniBand fat trees, and with Trainium's move from torus to switch.
teachback: NVLink gives every GPU in an NVL72 rack one hop to the other 71. An Ironwood chip has 6 neighbours and the pod has 9,216 chips. Argue for each design with numbers.
Why do you get roughly half the collective bandwidth on a 2×2×2 slice compared with a 4×4×4 cube?
What did Google change in TPU 8i's network, and why, given what decode traffic looks like?
Walk the bandwidth ladder for Ironwood from HBM to DCN and say which kind of parallelism belongs at each rung.

ch04.description: Transformer accounting for TPUs: parameter and FLOP counts, 6ND, KV cache size, attention intensity in prefill and decode, MoE batch requirements.
objectives: I can count the FLOPs of any einsum, and derive 6 × parameters × tokens for training from 2× forward and 4× backward.
I can count the parameters of a dense GQA transformer and of an MoE, split into MLP, attention and vocabulary.
I can compute KV-cache bytes per token and per sequence, and say how many sequences fit on a chip after the weights.
I can derive when attention FLOPs dominate (T > 8D) and why decode attention is never compute-bound.
I can compute the compute-bound batch for an MoE layer and explain why it is E/k times larger than for a dense layer.
I can estimate training memory (10 bytes per parameter plus activations) and show that large clusters are needed for FLOPs, not memory.
I can name the TPU-specific consequences of model shape — padding to 256, head dimension, KV heads — and where they show up later.
teachback: Estimate on a whiteboard, in two minutes, the FLOPs and the Ironwood-pod-days to train a 70B dense model on 15T tokens.
Why does an MoE make decode harder to make compute-bound, and by what factor?
A 70B model has 320 KB of bf16 KV cache per token. How many 32k-token conversations fit beside the weights on 8 Ironwood chips?
Why is decode attention memory-bound at every batch size, while the MLP becomes compute-bound at large enough batch?

ch05.description: Sharded matmuls and collectives on a TPU torus: sharding notation, the four matmul cases, AllGather, ReduceScatter, AllReduce and AllToAll costs.
objectives: I can read and write sharding notation, such as A[I_X, J_Y] and the unreduced marker {U_X}, and the equivalent JAX PartitionSpec. I can say what each device holds for a given mesh and spec.
I can classify any sharded matmul into the four cases and name the collective each needs.
I can derive the bidirectional-ring AllGather time V / W_ici and explain why it does not depend on the number of chips. I can extend it to several axes, to AllReduce (2×) and to AllToAll (¼).
I can say when a collective is latency-bound, and compute the threshold on v5e and Ironwood.
I can explain collective matmul (decomposing an AllGather into collective-permutes overlapped with partial matmuls) and compare it with async tensor parallelism on GPUs.
I can relate the book's formulas to NCCL's algbw and busbw, and compare how quickly TPU and GPU collectives reach peak bandwidth.
teachback: Why doesn't AllGather time on a ring depend on how many chips are in the ring?
Explain to a Megatron user what XLA's collective matmul does, and what they would have to do on a GPU to get the same overlap.
Given A[B, D] sharded P('X', 'Y') and W[D, F] sharded P('Y', None), what happens and what does it cost on an Ironwood 4×4×4 cube?
Why is an AllToAll a quarter of an AllGather on a TPU ring, and what does that mean for MoE?

ch06.description: Choosing a training mesh on TPU: data parallel, FSDP, tensor and pipeline parallelism thresholds, LLaMA-3 on v5p and Ironwood, GPU recipes compared.
objectives: I can derive the condition under which each training scheme is compute-bound — data parallelism, FSDP, tensor parallelism, FSDP plus TP, and cross-slice data parallelism over DCN.
I can compute the optimal FSDP degree, X_opt, and pick a mesh for a given model, batch and slice.
I can redo the Scaling Book's LLaMA-3-70B plan on a v5p pod, and explain why the same batch is communication-bound on a full Ironwood pod.
I can explain why pipeline parallelism is central to GPU recipes and secondary on TPUs, citing LLaMA-3's actual GPU configuration.
I can map these choices to MaxText configuration — ici_* against dcn_* axes and logical axis rules.
teachback: Give the one-line rule for when FSDP stops being free, with the number for v5p and for Ironwood.
Why did Meta use 16-way pipeline parallelism for LLaMA-3 405B on GPUs, when a TPU pod would mostly not?
Choose a mesh for a 70B dense model on a 2,048-chip Ironwood slice with a 4M-token batch, and say whether it is compute-bound.
What would you change if your Ironwood training run is communication-bound and you cannot raise the batch?

ch07.description: LLM inference on TPU: prefill vs decode rooflines, KV-cache-bound decode, batch breakeven, decode sharding, fp8 and int8 quantization with Qwix.
objectives: I can state the decode step-time lower bound and the general step-time formula, and compute both for a model on a slice.
I can compute the compute-bound decode batch for each weight and math precision on v5e, Ironwood, 8i and H100, and explain why KV growth makes it unreachable at long context.
I can explain why prefill is compute-bound and decode is not, and what that implies for disaggregated serving and the prefill-to-decode server ratio.
I can choose a decode sharding — model parallelism up to F/(Bβ), the KV cache split by heads then by batch, never FSDP — and say when its collectives are latency-bound.
I can explain int8, fp8 and fp4 weights, activations and KV on TPU, say which generations have native fp8, and describe how Qwix applies post-training quantization.
I can explain speculative decoding as spending idle FLOPs in a memory-bound step.
teachback: Your PM wants 2× decode throughput on the same chips. List what moves the number and by how much — batch, fp8 weights, fp8 KV, more TP, speculative decoding.
Why is FSDP an order-of-magnitude regression for decode, when it is free for training?
At 32k context, why does 8i's FP8 peak barely matter for decode, and what does matter?
How many prefill servers do you need per decode server for 8k prompts and 512-token answers, and why?

ch08.description: The TPU serving stack: vLLM on TPU, tpu-inference, torchax, vllm-torchtpu, Ragged Paged Attention, static-shape continuous batching, KV layout.
objectives: I can describe how TPU serving got from JetStream through PyTorch/XLA and tpu-inference to the October 2026 split, and say which path to use for a new PyTorch or JAX port.
I can explain what torchax does to a torch.nn.Linear call, why tpu-inference needs the model as a pure function that returns its KV cache, and where the code ends up as HLO.
I can explain how continuous batching survives a compiler that wants static shapes — padded shape buckets compiled ahead, a flattened token batch, and Ragged Paged Attention's three sub-kernels.
I can read the tpu-inference KV-cache layout and explain its packing dimension from (8,128) tiling.
I can map tpu-inference's mesh axes to the decode sharding rules of Chapter 7.
I can size a deployment from the Scaling Book's LLaMA-3-70B serving analysis, and solve the book's 405B problem under a latency limit.
teachback: Explain to a vLLM-on-CUDA engineer how continuous batching works when every shape must be known at compile time.
What does torchax do to a torch.nn.Linear call, and where does it end up?
Why does the KV-cache tensor in tpu-inference have a 'packing' dimension?
You are porting a new PyTorch model to TPU this month. Which serving path do you choose and why?

ch09.description: From Python to the TPU MXU: jaxpr, StableHLO, XLA passes, Shardy, JAX sharding modes and shard_map, and TorchTPU's architecture in detail.
objectives: I can trace a function from Python through jaxpr, StableHLO, HLO and XLA's passes to LLO and TPU instructions, and dump each stage.
I can say what I control on TPU — shardings, constraints, layouts, remat, donation, flags and Pallas — and what I do not.
I can explain Shardy against GSPMD, compare JAX's three sharding modes (auto, explicit, manual shard_map), and say when to drop to each.
I can compare XLA whole-program compilation with CUDA Graphs and torch.compile with Inductor.

I can explain TorchTPU in detail — the PrivateUse1 backend, deferred StableHLO ops, its three eager modes, torch.compile without Inductor, the compile cache, tpu_dist and the SPMD handshake, and Pallas through jax_op.
I can contrast TorchTPU with JAX, torchax and PyTorch/XLA, and the TPU stack with AWS's Neuron stack.
teachback: A CUDA engineer says 'XLA is just CUDA Graphs.' Correct them in three sentences.
Draw how y = model(x) reaches the TPU under JAX jit, torchax, TorchTPU strict eager and TorchTPU torch.compile.
Why did TorchTPU need an 'SPMD handshake' that JAX never needed?
XLA inserted a giant AllGather you did not expect. What are your three options, from least to most effort?

ch10.description: Writing Pallas TPU kernels and profiling with XProf: BlockSpecs, VMEM tiling, reading traces and HLO ops, plus a full inference design review.
objectives: I can write and explain a Pallas TPU kernel — grid, BlockSpec index maps, the (8,128) rule, memory spaces, implicit double buffering, dimension_semantics and scratch accumulators — and say how it reaches the hardware through Mosaic.
I can choose a Pallas tile size from arithmetic intensity and the VMEM budget.
I can say when a Pallas kernel is worth writing on TPU and when XLA already does the job.
I can capture a TPU profile from JAX and from tpu-inference, and read the Trace Viewer, including async -start/-done pairs.
I can decode an HLO op line — shape, layout, tiling, memory space, fusion kind, called computation and replica groups.
I can find a communication-overlap failure and a sharding mistake in a profile, and use the op profile and roofline tools to choose what to fix.
I can run a design review — model, chip, SLO, mesh, quantization, batch, expected step time — and state the bottleneck in one sentence.
teachback: Show me in this trace where communication failed to overlap, and what you would change.
What is the Pallas equivalent of a CUDA thread block, and why is the answer that there isn't one?
Read this HLO line aloud, and tell me which memory the output lives in and how many bytes it really occupies.
Walk through the design review for LLaMA-3-70B on Ironwood under a 30 ms per-token limit at 32k context.

ch11.description: TPU vs GPU vs Trainium architecture: compute, memory, NVLink vs ICI torus, collectives, software stacks, and which workloads favour each design.
objectives: I can state the design bet behind GPUs, TPUs and Trainium, and what each gives up.

I can compare current chips quantitatively — compute per precision, HBM capacity and bandwidth, ridge point and on-chip memory — for Ironwood, TPU 8t and 8i, H100, B200, GB200, Rubin, Trainium2 and Trainium3.
I can compare scale-up and scale-out designs, and derive their consequences for AllGather and AllToAll and for training thresholds.
I can compare the programming models — kernels, compilation, PyTorch paths and partitioning.
I can say, for a given workload, which design has the structural advantage, and why.
I can name the 2025–26 convergence trends and the evidence for each.
teachback: In five minutes, explain to a room of CUDA engineers what a TPU gives up relative to a GPU, what it gets in return, and how to tell which side of that trade their workload is on.
Why can a TPU pod reach about 9,000 chips without packet switches while NVLink stops at 72, and what does each topology make cheap or expensive?
Blackwell added Tensor Memory and single-thread MMA issue. Argue whether GPUs are converging on TPU design, with the evidence for and against.
For an MoE model with 256 experts, which interconnect would you want for training, and why?
